topic.title: Managing a Translation Job
topic.shortdesc: How to monitor a translation job, bring its results into your workspace, and manage it from the job card.

body.p: Whether you are translating a project for the first time or running an incremental update, you monitor and manage every translation job in the same way, from a card in your workspace.
Each translation job appears as a card. While the job is pending or running, the card shows the current step and a progress indicator, and you can stop the job directly from the card.

When a job finishes, select Bring into Workspace on the card to add its translated files to your workspace for review. If a job fails partway through, any output that it managed to produce before failing is still packaged as an importable artifact. You can bring this partial output into your workspace by using Bring partial results into workspace, so a failed job is not necessarily a total loss. You can also use the card's overflow menu to remove the job.

p.note: While a translation job is running, do not make other changes in the same workspace to the source or target files that it covers. Concurrent edits can conflict with the files that the agent is about to write, and the translation job does not track those changes.

section.title: Checking the Job Log
section.p: Every job that starts running keeps an execution log. You can open it from the card by using one of these controls:

ul.li: View log - Opens the Execution log dialog. While the job is running, the log updates live. After the job finishes, it shows the final log.
Download log - Saves the full log as a text file, for example, to attach when you contact support.

section.p: The most common reason to open the log is to find out why a job failed. A failed job card shows only a short failure message, while the log records the underlying cause.
For example, a job can fail when your organization has run out of AI credits. In that case, the log reports an AI credits exhausted error.

fig.title: Execution Log of a Failed Job

section.p: The log is also one of the two places where the agent can provide its answer when you ask it a question instead of asking it to translate.

section.title: Tracking Which Jobs You Have Brought into Your Workspace
section.p: When you have many finished jobs, it can be difficult to tell which ones you have already brought into your workspace. After you select Bring into Workspace, the job is marked with an Integrated badge, and its tooltip shows when it was brought in.

If you need to bring the same job in again (for example, after you discarded the changes), select Mark as not integrated from the card's overflow menu. This clears the badge and restores the Bring into Workspace action.
